tagline: Global leader in information management services trusted by 240,000+ customers across 61 countries
hero_kpi_rationale: Physical storage revenue is the historical and structural pillar of IRM, representing over 58% of revenue and powered by a stable and recurring installed base, driving robust organic growth of 9.6% in 2025.

kpis.name: Storage rental revenue
kpis.explanation: Money earned by leasing space to store physical documents and host data infrastructure.
kpis.description: Physical storage revenue is advancing through better pricing management and stable demand, notably in regulated segments such as healthcare and finance. Organic growth of 9.6%.
kpis.signal: Recurring and growing pillar of the business

kpis.name: Service revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from services associated with storage, digitization, and asset management.
kpis.description: Growth sustained by new digital services, traditional document management activities, and acquisition in the ALM segment. Organic growth of 11.2%.
kpis.signal: Accelerated growth driven by digital services and ALM

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, adjusted for restructuring and transformation costs.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA grows 15.1%, driven by organic revenue growth and efficient management of operating costs, reaching 37.3% margin.
kpis.signal: Strong operational performance despite transformation costs

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA margin
kpis.explanation: Adjusted EBITDA divided by total revenue, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA margin increases from 36.4% in 2024 to 37.3% in 2025, reflecting sustained improvement in operational efficiency.

kpis.name: Capital expenditures
kpis.explanation: Investment spending for the acquisition or improvement of physical assets such as buildings, data centers, and IT systems.
kpis.description: The 10-K does not specify the total CAPEX amount for 2025, but the data reveals substantial investments in data centers and operational transformation.
kpis.signal: Significant investments in data centers and Project Matterhorn

kpis.name: Total headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the company at the end of the period.
kpis.description: The number of employees is not disclosed in the 10-K, but the company conducted significant headcount reductions as part of Project Matterhorn.
kpis.signal: Restructuring in progress via Project Matterhorn

kpis.name: Restructuring and transformation costs
kpis.explanation: Expenses related to company restructuring and operational transformation via Project Matterhorn.
kpis.description: Restructuring costs related to Project Matterhorn reached $195.9 million in 2025, up 21.3% from $161.4 million in 2024. Total cumulative investment since 2022: $574.4 million.
kpis.signal: Significant investment in comprehensive transformation completed in 2025

kpis.name: Total assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of €21.13 billion in the latest year

kpis.name: Total revenue
kpis.description: Consolidated annual revenue, values extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 fiscal years of declared 10-K filings.
kpis.signal: Revenue of $6.902 billion in the latest year

kpis.name: Net income
kpis.description: Consolidated annual net income, values extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 fiscal years of declared 10-K filings.
kpis.signal: Net income of $0.152 billion in the latest year

kpis.name: Organic growth
kpis.explanation: Revenue growth excluding acquisitions and currency effects, measuring intrinsic performance.
kpis.description: Organic growth increases from 8.2% in 2024 to 10.2% in 2025, driven by digital services, data centers, and pricing management of physical storage.
kpis.signal: Robust and sustainable organic growth over two years

kpis.name: Project Matterhorn investments
kpis.explanation: Total costs incurred since the launch of the comprehensive transformation program in 2022 through its completion in 2025.
kpis.description: IRM invested $574.4 million cumulatively in Project Matterhorn since its launch in September 2022 through completion at year-end 2025. Program focused on optimization of the global operating model and acceleration of growth.

risks.title: Restructuring and transformation costs
risks.score_rationale: Restructuring costs related to the Matterhorn project totaled $574.4 million since 2022, with $195.9 million in 2025. While significant, the project is complete, which reduces future risk.

risks.title: Currency fluctuations
risks.score_rationale: Net foreign currency losses of $105.6 million in 2025, primarily related to GBP/EUR versus USD variations. Significant exposure due to international presence in 61 countries.

risks.title: Technology and cybersecurity dependence
risks.score_rationale: Data infrastructure and information management systems are critical for 240,000 customers. Vulnerability to cybersecurity risks, technical failures, and high maintenance costs.

risks.title: Increased competition in digital services
risks.score_rationale: Fragmented market with growing competition from new entrants and cloud providers. Risk of technology substitution for traditional physical storage services.

risks.title: Regulatory and compliance risks
risks.score_rationale: Subject to strict regulations (GDPR, HIPAA, etc.) across 61 countries. Potential high impact on operating costs and liability in case of non-compliance.

risks.title: Dependence on economic growth in addressable markets
risks.score_rationale: Revenue growth linked to economic cycles and demand for information services in regulated segments (finance, healthcare, insurance). Economic slowdown could impact volumes.

risks.title: Acquisition integration and returns
risks.score_rationale: Recent acquisitions in the ALM segment generating $87.5 million in incremental revenue. Risk of failure to realize expected synergies and complex operational integration.

ai_positioning.summary: Iron Mountain has no significant mentions concerning artificial intelligence, machine learning, or similar technologies in the provided excerpts from its 10-K/20-F document.
